newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO down on crude, Chinese buyers quiet.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO down on crude, Chinese buyers quiet.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices eased marginally on Wednesday as weaker crude dragged prices lower, traders said.
Traders said the market is still long and cargoes are still seeking homes.
A major oil company was heard to have offered at $121 per tonne for end November loading, 180-cst supplies but later dropped offers to $119.
Bids were very lacking, said another trader. "Very little Chinese bid were heard," he said.

Taiwan's tender to buy low sulphur fuel oil was heard to have been awarded to a western trader. A cargo each of 0.5 percent sulphur and 1.0 percent sulphur fuel oil was purchased at "low $140s" and $130-$135 per tonne respectively.
In the swaps market, November fuel oil was discussed at $118.50/$119.50, below Tuesday's quotes of $119/$119.75, tracking crude losses, trader said.
